signals.description: Tämä ei ole ennakkoilmoitus, tarjouspyyntö, hankintailmoitus tai kutsu neuvottelumenettelyyn, eikä ilmoituksen julkaisemisella aloiteta tarjouskilpailua. Mahdollinen hankintailmoitus ja tarjouspyyntö julkaistaan myöhemmin. Tietopyyntö ei velvoita hankintayksikköä toteuttamaan varsinaista hankintaa. Tällä tietopyynnöllä kartoitetaan markkinoita ja saadaan hankintaa koskevaa tietoa suunniteltaessa Helsingin kaupungin tekoälyn hallinnan järjestelmän hankintaa. Tämän tietopyynnön tavoitteena on saada tietoa markkinoilla olevista ratkaisuista, kyvykkyyksistä ja vaihtoehtoisista toteutustavoista ennen varsinaista mahdollista kilpailutusta. Helsingin kaupunki valmistelee hankintaa tekoälyn hallinnan järjestelmästä, jonka tarkoituksena on mahdollistaa EU:n tekoälyasetuksen (AI Act) mukaisten velvoitteiden hallinta ja dokumentointi sekä tukea kaupungin kaikkien tekoälyjärjestelmien elinkaaren aikaista hallintaa. Tekoälyn hallinnan järjestelmä mahdollistaa EU:n tekoälyasetuksen tarjoajan ja käyttöönottajan velvoitteiden hallinnan, osoittamisen ja raportoimisen suuririskisten tekoälyjärjestelmien osalta sekä tukee kaupungin kaikkien tekoälyjärjestelmien hallintaa, tekoälyriskien tunnistamista ja hallintaa sekä viestintää tekoälystä. Tekoälyn hallinnan järjestelmä tuottaa tietoa kaupungin johdolle, tekoälykehittäjille sekä tekoälyä hyödyntäviin kaupungin palveluihin sekä verkkosivuille. Järjestelmä toimii keskeisenä työkaluna riskien tunnistamisessa ja hallinnassa, dokumentoinnissa, viestinnän valmistelussa sekä käyttöönottoprosessien tukena. Lisätietoa hankinnan kohteesta on kuvattu liitteessä "Hankinnan kohteen kuvaus". OHJEET TIETOPYYNTÖÖN VASTAAMISEEN Pyydämme vastaamaan kirjallisesti liitteessä "Tietopyynnön kysymykset" ja "Ympäristökriteerit" esitettyihin kysymyksiin mahdollisimman kattavasti asetettuun määräaikaan mennessä. Pyydämme ilmoittamaan, mikäli vastaus näkemyksenne mukaan sisältää liikesalaisuuksia tai muuta salassa pidettävää tietoa. Pyydämme yksilöimään ja merkitsemään nämä tiedot selvästi. MARKKINAVUOROPUHELU Hankintayksikkö varaa oikeuden järjestää tietopyyntöön vastanneiden kanssa tarkentavia markkinavuoropuheluja harkintansa mukaan. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu keskustelemaan kaikkien vastanneiden kanssa. Hankintayksikkö järjestää toimittajakohtaiset markkinavuoropuhelut ensisijaisesti etäyhteyksin maalis-huhtikuussa 2026, mikäli ne katsotaan tarpeelliseksi. Toimittajakohtaiset kutsut markkinavuoropuheluun toimitetaan tietopyynnön määräajan jälkeen. Hankintayksikkö toimittaa mahdollisesti alustavat tarjouspyyntöasiakirjat kommentoitaviksi myöhemmin. Tietopyynnöllä ja markkinavuoropuhelulla kerätyt tiedot säilyvät luottamuksellisina ja niitä tullaan käyttämään ainoastaan hankinnan suunnitteluun. LISÄTIETOJA Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu tässä ilmoituksessa tai sen liitteissä ilmoitettuihin tietoihin, vaan valmistelun edetessä hankinnan kohde ja vaatimukset voivat muuttua. Tietopyynnössä annetut vastaukset eivät ole toimittajaa sitovia. Tietopyyntöön vastaaminen ei ole edellytys myöhempään mahdollisesti järjestettävään tarjouskilpailuun osallistumiselle. Tietopyyntöön vastaaminen tai vastaamatta jättäminen ei vaikuta mahdollisen toimittajan asemaan varsinaisessa tarjouskilpailussa. Tietopyyntöön vastaamisesta tai markkinavuoropuheluun osallistumisesta ei makseta korvausta. Alustavasti tarjouspyyntö on suunniteltu julkaistavaksi kesäkuun 2026 aikana.

signals.description: TÄMÄ EI OLE ENNAKKOILMOITUS, HANKINTAILMOITUS TAI TARJOUSPYYNTÖ VAAN ILMOITUS MARKKINAVUOROPUHELUN KÄYNNISTÄMISESTÄ OSANA HANKINNAN SUUNNITTELUA. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue kartoittaa Toimittajien kiinnostusta taloussuunnittelujärjestelmää koskevaan kilpailutukseen. Länsi-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialue (LUVN) vastaa alueensa sosiaali ja terveydenhuollon sekä pelastustoimen järjestämisestä. Hyvinvointialueella työskentelee noin 10 000 henkilöä, ja sen vuotuiset nettomenot ovat noin 2 miljardia euroa. Toimintaa johdetaan viiden palvelualueen ja neljänkymmenen palvelulinjan kokonaisuutena. Taloussuunnitteluun osallistuu vuosittain noin 400 henkilöä ja suunniteltava kokonaisuus kattaa noin 1 000 kustannuspaikkaa. Tämä tietopyyntö on osa markkinavuoropuhelua, jonka tavoitteena on kartoittaa markkinoilla olevia ratkaisuja taloussuunnittelun tueksi. Tietopyyntö ei ole hankintailmoitus, eikä se sido hyvinvointialuetta tai toimittajia myöhempiin menettelyihin. 1. HANKINNAN KOHDE JA TAVOITE LUVN suunnittelee taloussuunnittelujärjestelmän hankintaa, jonka avulla voidaan laatia talousarvio, taloussuunnitelmat, ennusteet ja muu talouden suunnittelu organisaation eri tasoilla. Tavoitteena on kartoittaa mahdollisuuksia parantaa talouden suunnittelun laatua, rullaavuutta, yhtenäisyyttä, läpinäkyvyyttä ja toimintavarmuutta hyvinvointialueen laajassa toiminnallisessa kokonaisuudessa. Tavoitteena on myös automatisoida prosesseja mm. tekoälyä hyödyntämällä. Järjestelmältä toivotaan muun muassa seuraavia ominaisuuksia: - Talousarvion ja ennusteiden laadinta - Henkilöstösuunnittelu: Suunnittelu toteutetaan HTV-perusteisesti niin, että lopputuotos sisältää sekä henkilöstösuunnitelman että euromääräisen budjetin - Sisäinen laskutus: kustannusten kohdistaminen ja laskutusprosessien tuki. Organisaatiossa toimii 3 vastuualuetta (Digipalvelut, Palvelukeskus, Tilapalvelut), joiden kulut laskutetaan aiheutumisperusteisesti muulle organisaatiolle. Kokonaisuus on merkittävä sekä taloudellisen vaikutuksen että vaaditun työmäärän suhteen - Ostopalvelusuunnittelu: muokattavat ajuripohjaiset laskentamallit ja suunnittelurakenteet - Laaja tuki laskentadimensioille: pakolliset ja vapaaehtoiset kirjausdimensiot - Laadukkaat tiedonsiirto- ja raportointiominaisuudet - Järjestelmän tulee tarjota rajapinta, jonka kautta data voidaan siirtää tiheällä päivitysvälillä asiakkaan tietokantaan 2. OSALLISTUMINEN MARKKINAVUOROPUHELUUN Toimittajia pyydetään osallistumaan markkinavuoropuheluun vastaamalla tähän tietopyyntöön. Pyydetyt tiedot annetaan lomakkeen kohdassa "Muut tiedot". signals.description: The term intends to enter into a contract for licences for the KI based tool Claude from the supplier Anthropic. Justification for the choice: The term needs an advanced, general KI-tool that can be used by employees across disciplines, including developers, designers and other roles. The aim is to support analysis, development and interaction assignments in line with Sikt's strategic targets for the use of artificial intelligence. After completed needs and market assessments, Visibility ́s assessment is that Claude currently appears to be the best suitable solution for the purpose, particularly in light of: *support for secure and final user-controlled access to data and integrations based on open standards, **good interaction between different user groups, including close collaboration between developers and other professional environments, technical prerequisites for integration with Sikt's existing platform services and architecture. Visibility has assessed alternative systems in the market, including, among other things, Copilot, Gemini, ChatGPT and Cursor, but they are not currently assessed to cover the need to a sufficient degree, especially in terms of the combination of access management, integration options and use across roles. The market for KI tools is developing quickly. The choice of Claude is therefore based on an assessment of available systems at the time of the procurement and is not intended to establish any type of long-term standardisation or supplier binding. Procurement form: The term has examined the possibility of acquiring Claude through the existing framework agreement for software licenses, but has been confirmed that the product cannot be delivered through it. Direct procurements from Anthropic are thus the only available procurement route. Extent and value of the procurement: The procurement concerns licences for Claude, with a staged and needs managed employee disclosure. The estimated total contract value is NOK 3,500,000. The actual cost will depend on the number of users and actual use over time. Options: No options.

signals.description: GENERAL This document is not a procurement announcement, not an Call for tenders, nor will its publication start a Tender Procurement Process. The purpose of this Pre-market consultation notice is to identify potential suppliers operating in the market and their offerings. Responding or not responding to this Pre-market consultation notice does not prevent participation in a possible future tender. This Pre-market consultation notice does not obligate the contracting authority to carry out an actual procurement procedure. All information presented in this Pre-market consultation notice is preliminary and indicative. Laurea University of Applied Sciences operates in five locations in the Uusimaa region in Finland. Laurea offers both bachelor’s and master’s degree studies but also open university studies, specialisation education and continuing education. The fields of study are Business Management, Information technology, Service business, Social Services, Nursing, Health Care and Hospitality Management. Laurea has approximately 9,900-degree students and approximately 13,000 Open UAS students per year as well as about 670 employees. PRELIMINARY SCOPE OF THE PROCUREMENT The scope of the procurement is a Software as a Service (SaaS) online exam proctoring system for Laurea UAS. The system must integrate with Laurea's learning platform (Canvas) and provide video and audio-based proctoring recorded and stored by the system. The procurement does not include a personal live monitoring service by the supplier or the use of artificial intelligence to monitor/check and identify suspected fraud. The procurement includes the deployment of the software service and support and maintenance services separately for each higher education institution. MARKET DIALOGUE The contracting authority reserves the right to engage in market dialogue with the responding companies regarding the planned procurement and the tender documents. In addition, the contracting authority reserves the right to conduct the potential market dialogue either in the form of written comments on the draft tender documents or through one-on-one meetings (via Teams or in person). The possibility to comment on the draft tender documents is preliminary planned to be arranged once before the publication of the final Call for tenders, regardless of the format. Any potential market dialogue will be conducted in English, and all related materials will be provided only in English. No compensation will be paid for participation in the market dialogue. Hansel Oy will act in a consultative role in the procurement process. REGISTRATION FOR THE MARKET DIALOGUE Potential service providers interested in participating in the dialogue are kindly asked to register via email as soon as possible and at the latest by 6 February 2026. Send the name and contact details of the interested service provider to maritta.riskila@laurea.fi. Use a reference "TD for an Online exam proctoring system" and the company name as the subject of the email. The service providers may register in Finnish or English.

signals.description: Welcome to the Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Expertise for the Control Room of the Future program and adjacent subjects. Note: This Dynamic Purchasing System is a continuation on the Mercell platform of the DPS that was previously operational on the Negometrix platform with Negometrix reference 159478 for which formal notice 2021/S 087-226573 was published on 5-May-2021 on the TED website. If your company was already qualified for participation on the Negometrix platform, a simplified procedure applies for re-establishing your qualification, see question 2.1 on the Mercell platform. TenneT will renew and innovate the (IT) systems that it uses for controlling and balancing its grids in the period 2021-2031. In connection with this, TenneT expects to be needing extensive external expertise, related to existing and new technologies and ways of working, in particular related to the challenges that TenneT faces in the energy transition. Compared to current ways of working, innovations will be needed to handle e.g. the increasing infeed of solar and wind energy that is far more difficult to predict and control than traditional generation. The subject of this tender procedure is a Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for expertise (including the development of algorithms and IT Tools) that TenneT needs in connection with the renewal of its (IT) systems related to the control and balancing of the electricity transmission grid. Initially, the DPS contains the following categories of expertise: 1. power system control and monitoring; 2. energy platforms and interconnected IT systems; 3. data analysis, artificial intelligence and machine learning; 4. system and process implementation. This Tender Dossier contains the rules for the Application by Economic operators for qualification under this DPS. In order to become qualified for one or more of the categories, the Economic operator has to fulfil all the requirements of this DPS. In addition, the Economic operator needs to the answer all Mercell questions, and submit the requested documents and-or evidence at the respective Mercell question with the submission of its Application. During the course of time, the specific assignments (contracts) under the DPS will be tendered for which all suppliers that have qualified for the particular category will be invited to submit an offer. Any interested supplier may at any moment during the lifetime of the DPS submit a request to be qualified for participating in the tender procedures for specific assignments within one or more of the categories of this DPS. Your request will be accepted if it satisfies the applicable requirements and if you accept the stated conditions. Once you have qualified, you will automatically receive a notification when TenneT publishes a request for proposal for a specific subject within a category for which you have qualified. TenneT emphasises that it would also like to attract small and medium sized companies to this DPS. Qualification requests will be processed by TenneT in the sequence of receipt. TenneT will inform you as soon as possible and endeavors to do so within 10 working days from the date of receipt about the acceptance or rejection of your qualification request. During the lifetime of the DPS, TenneT will be entitled to add new categories, to close existing categories, and to split-up existing categories in to one or more categories.

Sykehusinnkjøp HF hereby invites tenderers to a market dialogue for the procurement of a laboratory information system for the health companies in Helse Nord. The market dialogue is a part of the preliminary work for the procurement and is being carried out because the Contracting Authority would like input for the procurement from potential suppliers, possibly also from other interested parties. As a part of this process, suppliers are invited to provide input to the procurement prior to the announcement. The feedback makes it possible to make a decision about the type of procurement and procurement procedure. Based on input from the market dialogue, the Contracting Authority will, as needed, open to a closer dialogue with some of the suppliers for further details and discussions. The contracting authority would like input on the following points: Short presentation of the supplier/tendererWhich the specialist areas the system is meant to cover (see further information on all disciplines within the laboratory service in annex "Invitation to market dialogue") About the solution, including brief information on functionality, possibilities and limitations, and: Describe how the system is built up in the tender documentation. modules, and which advantages this provides. How the system is deployed to clients; web based and/or sw deployed on clients. By the latter; whether there are specific requirements for clients. How the system will be deployed back-end. Describe how the system supports portable devices (tablets etc.). References to customers where the system is in use (and possibly which parts of the system they use). The tenderer ́s thoughts on how the system will support future development within the disciplines, e.g. within AI, integrations (i.a. FHIR), personalised medicine, etc. Input for the procurement as regards the expected functionality described in chapter 5 (see annex "Invitation to Market Dialogue"):How does the system ensure user friendliness, intuitive user interface and training? How does the system cover the overall description and for each of the disciplines covered by the solution? If there is functionality that cannot be offered we would like to know this. Which disciplines the solution covers and whether it covers all disciplines within the laboratory service (note possible exceptions for transfusion medicine/blood bank). How the system supports decision support functionality. How the solution supports artificial intelligence. How the system supports personalised medicine. How does the system support different integration mechanisms with other systems (FHIR, message exchange in accordance with Norwegian requirements, etc.?) Delivery. Which factors affect delivery time and how do you handle risk? All the functionalities are ready developed and can be delivered. If there is functionality that needs to be developed, it is desirable to know. Delivery model: cloud and/or local installation. If the system is cloud compatible; about Norwegian requirements are complied with. Whether there are specific requirements for HW and underlying SW-platform for customers. Short proposals as to how the system will be implemented at Customer Provisions that the Customer is expected to fulfil. Frequency of release bicycles and response to new functionality and error recovery. Integrations: does this require assistance from customers? Describe the pricing model and what factors affect the total cost of ownership (TCO) Licenses Maintenance/support price driven factors. And input that the tenderer deems important. Deadline for written feedback on the above mentioned points from interested parties: 28.11.2025. This is only a prior information notice in order to get information on the market and to have a dialogue with relevant suppliers. The actual competition may be announced at a later date. Feedback on or questions to the market survey is done in the Mercell communication module. signals.description: El objeto del presente contrato son los SERVICIOS DE ANÁLISIS, DISEÑO, DESARROLLO E IMPLANTACIÓN DE UN SISTEMA DE COORDINACIÓN VIRTUAL DE AGENTES (CoVA) APLICADOS A LA ASITENCIA INTERGENERACIONAL PARA LA ADMINISTRACIÓN DEL PRINCIPADO DE ASTURIAS que permita una administración proactiva y eficiente, abarcando tanto los procesos como las personas y la tecnología necesaria para un adecuado uso, seguridad y manejo de la misma. Este contrato se enmarca en la Compra Pública de Tecnología Innovadora, (CPTI), su objeto tiene un contenido innovador y emplea especificaciones funcionales, y no requisitos técnicos: Se orienta a la adquisición de un servicio que no existe en el Principado de Asturias, pero puede desarrollarse en un tiempo razonable, dado que la tecnología está en un grado de desarrollo que así lo permite. Las tareas principales incluidas en este contrato son las siguientes: a. Implementación de un sistema de coordinación virtual de agentes basados en inteligencia artificial aplicados a la asistencia intergeneracional para la Administración del Principado de Asturias que permita el aprovechamiento de los datos generados y gestionados. b. Todos los servicios necesarios para la puesta en marcha de los elementos contratados, suscripciones/licencias necesarias, así como su gestión y mantenimiento durante la fase piloto de demostración. c. El aprovechamiento del potencial de los datos de la Administración del Principado de Asturias (en adelante, APA) para implementar nuevas formas de gestión pública basada en la interoperabilidad y analítica de datos. d. Establecer las bases tecnológicas y procedimentales para la implantación de una Administración proactiva que permita la optimización del gasto público maximizando su rendimiento. e. El desarrollo de técnicas/reglas para la gestión automatizada y clasificación de datos, documentos y expedientes mediante técnicas avanzadas de Inteligencia Artificial. f. La incorporación de técnicas de aprendizaje profundo (Deep Learning) ya que en estos procesos de digitalización pueden producir inmensas cantidades de datos para el entrenamiento y así poder dar un procesamiento que incremente la eficiencia, la eficacia y la inteligencia en el tratamiento de los datos en los procesos de las Administraciones Públicas. g. La creación de un espacio de datos corporativo que incluya los datos en origen, aquellos que se hayan podido inferir durante en el ámbito de uso del sistema, así como facilitar la interoperabilidad y circuitos de tramitación administrativa. h. signals.description: Tietopyynnön tarkoituksena on kartoittaa markkinoilla olevia tiedolla johtamisen asiantuntijapalveluja, AI-avusteiset asiantuntijapalveluja sekä AI-agenttikirjastoja tuottavia toimijoita sekä vaihtoehtoja. Tietopyynnön tavoitteena on varmistaa Keusoten käyttöön riittävät ja osaavat tiedolla johtamisen asiantuntijapalvelut, AI-avusteiset asiantuntijapalvelut sekä Keusoten asiantuntijaresursseille tarjottava AI-agenttikirjasto vuosille 2026–2029. Tietopyyntö ei velvoita Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialuetta toteuttamaan hankintaa tietopyynnössä tai sen liitteissä kuvatulla tavalla ja tarjouskilpailu voidaan myös jättää toteuttamatta. Tässä ilmoituksessa esitetyt tiedot ja kuvaukset ovat alustavia ja suuntaa antavia ennakkotietoja, jotka eivät sido Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialuetta. Kyseessä on vain tietopyyntö eikä se johda selvityksessä olevan ratkaisun kilpailutukseen vaan hankintaprosessi käynnistetään erillisellä päätöksellä. Tietopyynnön vastaukset tulee toimittaa suomen kielellä. Tulevan kilpailutuksen onnistumisen varmistamiseksi on tärkeää, että tarjoajat antavat hankintayksikölle mahdollisimman laajasti pyydettyjä tietoja. Kaikki tietopyynnössä saadut tiedot käsitellään luottamuksellisesti. Tietopyyntöön vastaaminen ei ole edellytys kilpailutukseen osallistumiselle. signals.description: Udbudsprocessen omfatter indgåelse af én (1) kontrakt vedrørende Ordregivers anskaffelse af udvikling af et AI-baseret simulationsredskab til træning af børnesamtaler. På baggrund af nærværende udbud vil der blive indgået én (1) fælles kontrakt mellem leverandøren og den Ansvarlige Ordregiver, jf. udbudsbetingelsernes punkt 1.2, som handler på vegne af samtlige deltagende ordregivere. Den Ansvarlige Ordregiver er Professionshøjskolen Absalon, som er bemyndiget til at varetage samtlige rettigheder og forpligtelserne i henhold til kontrakten og optræder som kontraktpart over for leverandøren. Leverandøren kan således alene rette krav mod den Ansvarlige Ordregiver. Øvrige deltagende ordregivere er ikke direkte kontraktparter og hæfter hverken individuelt eller solidarisk for opfyldelsen af kontrakten. Professionshøjskolen Absalon udbyder i samarbejde med de øvrige professionshøjskoler, Red Barnet, Barndom Uden Vold og Ole Kirk’s Fond en opgave om udvikling af et AI-baseret simulationsredskab, som i udbudsmaterialet betegnes Løsningen. Formålet er at styrke socialrådgiveres og socialrådgiverstuderendes kompetencer til at gennemføre samtaler med børn i sårbare situationer, herunder børn der kan have været udsat for vold eller overgreb. Løsningen skal skabe et realistisk, trygt og læringsorienteret træningsmiljø, hvor brugerne kan forberede sig på børnesamtaler, gennemføre samtaler med digitale avatarer, få vejledning og feedback fra en Tutor og efterfølgende analysere deres samtaler med henblik på læring og refleksion. Den skal både kunne anvendes i socialrådgiveruddannelsen, i efter- og videreuddannelsesforløb og i den kommunale praksis. Den første version, som dette udbud omfatter, skal give mulighed for tale- og tekstbaseret interaktion med fire avatarer i alderen 9–11 år, som repræsenterer forskellige baggrunde og sagstyper. Hertil kommer en Tutor, der understøtter brugeren før, under og efter samtalen gennem forberedende information, løbende faglige hints og efterfølgende debriefing. Løsningen skal rumme både fulde samtaleforløb og kortere moduler, hvor enkelte samtaleteknikker kan trænes isoleret. På længere sigt er ambitionen at udvide løsningen med mere avancerede modaliteter såsom mimik og kropssprog samt realtidsanalyse af nonverbal kommunikation. Ordregiver ønsker derfor at tiltrække leverandører, som ikke alene kan levere den udbudte løsning, men også kan tænke visionært i forhold til at skabe en fremtidssikret og innovativ platform. Den Ansvarlige Ordregiver stiller et omfattende vidensgrundlag til rådighed i form af praksisnære cases, anonymiserede børnesamtaler og fagpersoners ekspertise, og vil desuden bidrage aktivt med faglig sparring under udviklingen. Tilbuddene vil blive vurderet på realiserbarhed og risikovurdering, funktionalitet og sikkerhed, realismen i avatarerne, tutorens faglige kvalitet samt den samlede brugeroplevelse og tekniske robusthed. Den Ansvarlige Ordregiver er berettiget til at opsige kontrakten ved Delleverancedag 1 (POC), udelukkende med henblik på at kunne bringe projektet til ophør, såfremt det under Delleverance 1 - POC viser sig, at der foreligger tekniske udfordringer, som gør det umuligt at udvikle en egnet og anvendelig Løsning til det formål, som kontrakten understøtter, jf. Kontraktens punkt 31.2.1. Det er dog den Ansvarlige Ordregivers klare hensigt at gennemføre udviklingen af en fuldstændig Løsning, der fungerer efter sit formål. Af hensyn til fastlagt budget har Ordregiver fastlagt et prisloft for Leverancevederlaget. Leverancevederlaget, herunder prisen for Afklaringsfasen og Leverancen, jf. Kontraktbilag 01 – Tidsplan, må således maksimalt være fem (5) mio. DKK ekskl. moms. Inden for det fastlagte prisloft på fem (5) mio. DKK ekskl. moms ønsker Ordregiver at fremme løsninger, der kombinerer høj teknisk kvalitet og innovationshøjde. Med dette udbud tilstræber Ordregiver at understøtte en konkurrence, der ikke alene baseres på pris, men også på Tilbudsgivernes evne til at tænke langsigtet og visionært. Ordregiver redegør derfor for de strategiske og teknologiske ambitioner for Løsningen med henblik på at opfordre tilbudsgivere til at præsentere forslag, der afspejler en fremtidssikret og teknologisk avanceret tilgang. Samtidig er det vigtigt for Ordregiver, at Løsningen kan driftes bæredygtigt inden for de økonomiske rammer, der gælder for professionshøjskolernes fælles drift. Ordregiver ønsker derfor at indgå kontrakt med en Leverandør, der kan sikre iderigdom og teknisk snilde i forhold til at udvikle en Løsning, der opfylder de ønskede behov, men som samtidig kan driftes af professionshøjskolerne i fællesskab - hvor samtaleflow vægtes højere end visualisering af barnets nonverbale sprog.

signals.description: Die Auftraggeber führen einen wettbewerblichen Dialog zur Entwicklung eines Chatbots für das Bergische Servicecenter sowie für die Verwaltungen der drei Auftraggeber nach den Regelungen der Vergabeverordnung (VgV) durch. Mit der Ausschreibung soll für das Bergische Servicecenter sowie für die drei Auftraggeber ein Chatbot entwickelt werden, mit dem unter anderem sowohl die Angebote des Bergischen ServiceCenters als auch die Angebote der Verwaltungen der Städte Remscheid, Solingen und Wuppertal auf der Ebene der Informationsbereitstellung gegenüber der Bevölkerung und die Interaktion bzgl. der Verwaltungsleistungen der drei Städte ausgeführt bzw. wahrgenommen werden soll. Zukünftig soll der Chatbot entsprechend des aktuellen Stands der Technik weiterentwickelt werden, insbesondere auf der Interaktions- und Transaktionsebene sowie auch zur internen Verwaltungsunterstützung. Die Auftraggeber sollen sowohl gemeinsam für das Bergische Servicecenter als auch jeweils einzeln berechtigt sein, Leistungen vom Auftraggeber hinsichtlich des entwickelten Chatbots abrufen zu können (vgl. Vertragsentwurf, Anlage C zum 2. Verfahrensbrief). Auftragsgegenstand ist die Entwicklung eines Chatbotsystems zur Erfüllung von Serviceauf-gaben bzw. Angeboten des Bergischen Servicecenters auf der Ebene der Informationsbereitstellung gegenüber der Bevölkerung der Städte Remscheid, Solingen und Wuppertal. In den Lösungskonzepten ist bezüglich des Funktionsumfangs des Chatbots die zukünftig wei-tere Entwicklung der Interaktions- und Transaktionsebene sowie die Möglichkeit der internen Verwaltungsunterstützung zu berücksichtigen. Weiterhin ist Gegenstand des Auftrags auch die Pflege, Weiterentwicklung und Anpassung des Chatbotsystems. Das Chatbotsystem soll zum einen im Rahmen der Informationsbereitstellung für Bürger, Unternehmen und andere Informationssuchende insbesondere direkte Auskünfte zu verfüg-baren Dienstleistungen, Weiterleitungen zu entsprechenden Leistungen und Informationen sowie perspektivisch auf Interaktions- und Transaktionsebene unter anderem Beratungen zu Dienstleistungen umsetzen können. Hinsichtlich der internen Verwaltung sollen zum anderen perspektivisch durch das Chatbotsystem unteranderem die Textverwaltung, Rechercheassistenten und ein interner Servicebot unterstützt werden. Der Chatbot soll insbesondere multilingual, als KI-gestütztes Large-Language-Model, mit transparenter, widerspruchsfreier und freundlicher bzw. bürgernaher Sprache, mit stetiger Angabe von Quellen sowie unter Beachtung von datenschutz- und IT-sicherheitsrechtlicher Konformität umgesetzt werden.

signals.description: Keski-Uudenmaan hyvinvointialueen TKIO hankintajärjestelmä (jatkossa hankintajärjestelmä) muodostaa hankintayksikön tutkimus-, kehitys-, innovaatio- ja osaamisen kehittämisen toiminnan keskeisen osan ja hankinta-alustan. Se muodostaa tilaajan ja tutkimus-, kehittämis- ja innovaatiokumppanien sopimuksella säädellyn yhteistyömallin rakenteen. Hankintajärjestelmässä kilpailutettavien palvelujen tarkoituksena on tuottaa tuottavat tutkimustietoa, kehittämispalveluita ja innovaatioita tilaajan kehittämistoiminnan ja johtamisen perustaksi. Hankintajärjestelmä on jaettu luokkiin seuraavasti: Luokka 1 Innovaatiopalvelut Luokka 2 Palvelujärjestelmien kehittäminen Luokka 3 Hankepalvelut Luokka 4 Strateginen kehittäminen Luokka 5 Tiedeyhteisöt Lisäksi hankinnan kohteena ovat pilotointi- ja kokeilupalvelut sekä jatkuvan kehittämisen ja hallinnoinnin palvelut tilaajan käyttöön. Hankinnan kohde ja hankintajärjestelmän toiminta on kuvattu tarkemmin liitteessä ”TKIO dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän periaatteet”. Kunkin luokan vähimmäisvaatimukset sekä hakijoita koskevat perustamisvaiheen osaamisvaatimukset kuvataan tarkemmin tässä osallistumispyynnössä. Tilaaja määrittelee kussakin hankintajärjestelmän sisäisessä tarjouspyynnössä tarkemmin hankintajärjestelmässä kilpailutettavien toimeksiantojen kohteen ja vaatimukset. Hankintajärjestelmä on voimassa 31.10.2029 saakka, minä aikana hankintajärjestelmän sisäiset tarjouskilpailut tehdään. Tilaaja voi jatkaa hankintajärjestelmän voimassaoloa uudella hankintailmoituksella. Toimittajat voivat hakeutua hankintajärjestelmään perustamisvaiheessa ja myöhemmin sen voimassaoloaikana jättämällä osallistumishakemuksen osallistumispyynnön mukaisesti. Hankintamenettely on kaksivaiheinen. Päästäkseen jättämään tarjouksia toimittajan on ensin jätettävä osallistumishakemus ja tultava hyväksytyksi hankintajärjestelmään. Tämän jälkeen toimittaja voi tehdä tarjouksia vastaamalla hankintayksikön lähettämään tarjouspyyntöön. Hankintayksikkö toteuttaa jatkossa sisäisiä kilpailutuksia hankintajärjestelmässä tarpeen mukaan. Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään voi jättää osallistumishakemuksia koko sen keston ajan. Dynaamiseen hankintajärjestelmään otetaan mukaan kaikki soveltuvuusvaatimukset täyttävät hakijat. Varsinaiset hankinnat tehdään dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän sisäisillä kilpailutuksilla, joissa kuvataan ja tarkennetaan hankinnan kohde. DPS:n sisäisiin tarjouskilpailuihin ei voi osallistua, ellei toimittajaa ole hyväksytty hankintajärjestelmään. Osallistumishakemuksen jättäminen ja hankintajärjestelmään hyväksyminen ei velvoita toimittajaa tekemään tarjousta, vaan toimittajat voivat tehdä tarjouksia harkintansa mukaan. Hankintayksikkö arvioi osallistumispyynnön julkaisuhetkellä dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän kohteena olevien suunniteltujen hankintojen arvonlisäverottomaksi arvioiduksi määräksi 5,6 miljoonaa euroa huomioiden kaikki järjestelmässä mahdollisesti tehdyt hankinnat. Arvio on alustava ja perustuu tällä hetkellä tiedossa olevaan hankintatarpeeseen. Hankintayksikkö ei sitoudu mihinkään hankintamääriin tai määräostovelvoitteisiin tällä ilmoituksella. Luokassa 1 Innovaatiopalveluihin kuuluu innovaatioiden tuottaminen ja tulevaisuustutkimus. Innovaatiopalveluiden tarkoituksena on tuottaa tilaajalle innovatiivisia ratkaisuja ja uusia menetelmiä palvelujen järjestämiseksi ja tuottamiseksi vaikuttavalla tavalla. Innovaatiolla voidaan myös pyrkiä esimerkiksi palveluiden kysynnän ja sisällöllisten muutostarpeiden ennakointiin. Innovaatioita ovat esimerkiksi digitaaliset toimintamallit, teknologian innovatiiviseen hyödyntämiseen liittyvät ratkaisut tai robotiikan ja tekoälyn hyödyntäminen sosiaali- ja terveyspalveluissa. Innovaatioissa keskeistä on asiakaskokemuksen, laadun, vaikuttavuuden ja kustannusten näkökulmien huomioiminen. Innovaatiot voivat liittyä myös toiminnan seurantamalleihin, tulosten mittaamiseen tai strategiseen työhön. Innovaation tuloksena voi syntyä myös kaupallistettava tuote tai palvelu. Luokan 1 Innovaatiopalveluihin sisältyy lisäksi Pilotointi- ja kokeilupalvelut, joiden tarkoituksena on kokeilla uusia, toimeksiantojen tai muun yhteistyön tuloksena syntyneitä innovaatioita ja palveluja käytännössä. Jatkuva kehittäminen ja hallinnointi, jonka tarkoituksena on toimeksiantojen tuloksena syntyneiden uusien tai uudelleen muotoiltujen palveluiden, järjestelmien tai toimintojen toteutus siten, että toteutukseen sisältyy niiden jatkuva kehittäminen osana palvelutuotantoa tai muuta tilaajan toimintaa. Katso tarkemmin liite ”TKIO dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän periaatteet”.; Luokassa 2 Palvelujärjestelmien kehittäminen on asiantuntijapalvelua, jonka tarkoituksena on palvelujen, palveluprosessien, palvelujen verkostojen ja palvelujärjestelmien kehittäminen. Palvelujärjestelmien kehittämiseen kuuluu tiedon kerääminen ja analyysi nykytilasta ja tarpeista ja palveluiden vaikuttavuudesta. Tietoa hyödynnetään kehittämistoiminnassa. Palvelujärjestelmien kehittämiseen voi kuulua erilaisten menetelmien ja työkalujen tuottaminen tilaajan tarpeisiin muutosten toteuttamisen tueksi. Palveluun voi sisältyä sidosryhmäosallisuuden toteuttamista esimerkiksi palvelumuotoilun tai vastaavin keinoin. Palvelujärjestelmien kehittämiseen voi sisältyä myös valmennuksellista palvelua, jonka tarkoituksena on tukea tilaajaa kehittämistoiminnassa ja tulosten vakiinnuttamisessa. Luokan 2 Palvelujärjestelmien kehittämiseen sisältyy lisäksi - Pilotointi- ja kokeilupalvelut, joiden tarkoituksena on kokeilla uusia, toimeksiantojen tai muun yhteistyön tuloksena syntyneitä innovaatioita ja palveluja käytännössä. - Jatkuva kehittäminen ja hallinnointi, jonka tarkoituksena on toimeksiantojen tuloksena syntyneiden uusien tai uudelleen muotoiltujen palveluiden, järjestelmien tai toimintojen toteutus siten, että toteutukseen sisältyy niiden jatkuva kehittäminen osana palvelutuotantoa tai muuta tilaajan toimintaa. Katso tarkemmin liite ”TKIO dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän periaatteet”.; Luokan 3 Hankepalvelut pitää sisällään tilaajan tutkimus-, kehittämis- ja innovaatiotoimintaan liittyvien hankkeiden hankeprosessin hallinnoinnin kokonaisuuden. Hankepalveluihin kuuluvat hankesuunnittelupalvelut, hankejohtopalvelut ja projektipalvelut. Luokan 3 Hankepalveluihin sisältyy lisäksi - Pilotointi- ja kokeilupalvelut, joiden tarkoituksena on kokeilla uusia, toimeksiantojen tai muun yhteistyön tuloksena syntyneitä innovaatioita ja palveluja käytännössä. - Jatkuva kehittäminen ja hallinnointi, jonka tarkoituksena on toimeksiantojen tuloksena syntyneiden uusien tai uudelleen muotoiltujen palveluiden, järjestelmien tai toimintojen toteutus siten, että toteutukseen sisältyy niiden jatkuva kehittäminen osana palvelutuotantoa tai muuta tilaajan toimintaa. Katso tarkemmin liite ”TKIO dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän periaatteet”.; Luokan 4 Strategisen kehittämisen konsultointi on asiantuntijapalvelua, jonka tarkoituksena on mahdollistaa tilaajalle kokonaisvaltainen tuki kehittämistoimintaan ja muutoshallintaan, järjestäjäohjauksen ja palvelutuotannon näkökulmista. Strategisen kehittämisen konsultointi tuottaa monipuolista ja kokonaisvaltaista tietoa, osaamista ja näkemyksiä sosiaali- ja terveyspalveluiden sekä erikoissairaanhoidon kehittämisestä ja laajoista integrointihankkeista. Konsultointi tarjoaa asiantuntijaosaamista sosiaalihuollon, terveyspalveluiden ja erikoissairaanhoidon innovaatio- ja kehittämistoiminnan vaikuttavuuden, asiakaslähtöisyyden ja laadun edistämiseen sekä uusien toimintamallien ja prosessien kokonaisuuksien suunnitteluun, analysointiin ja käyttöönottoon. Strategisen kehittämisen konsultoinnin asiantuntijapalveluun kuuluu monipuolinen osaaminen sosiaali- ja terveyspalveluiden vaikuttavuuden ja tuottavuuden parantamisesta, rahoitusjärjestelmistä, palveluiden saavutettavuuden parantamisesta, palvelujärjestelmien ja verkostojen suunnittelusta, tiedolla johtamisen kyvykkyyden kehittämisestä ja tulevaisuuden ennakoinnista. Strateginen kehittäminen voi sisältää myös palvelutuotannon ohjauspalvelua, jonka avulla voidaan saavuttaa merkittäviä kustannussäästöjä, kun hankintasopimusten mukaista palvelutuotantoa ja tuottajakenttää saadaan ohjattua systemaattisemmin ja tavoitteellisemmin. Palvelutuotannon ohjauspalvelu voi myös auttaa hankintayksikköä löytämään palveluntuottajien johtamiseen johdonmukaiset ja monistettavissa olevat toimintaprosessit, joiden avulla voidaan saavuttaa palvelujen parempaa vaikuttavuutta, asiakastyytyväisyyttä, laatua ja kustannustehokkuutta. Katso tarkemmin liite ”TKIO dynaamisen hankintajärjestelmän periaatteet”.; Luokan 5 Tiedeyhteisöille hankintajärjestelmä toimii yhteistyöalustana ja hankintakanavana tiedeyhteisöihin, kuten yliopistoihin, korkeakouluihin, oppilaitoksiin, osaamiskeskuksiin ja tutkimuslaitoksiin päin. Hankintajärjestelmässä tiedeyhteisöiltä hankittava palvelu voi pitää sisällään tieteelliseksi toiminnaksi katsottavia palveluita, jotka sisällöltään täydentävät TKIO yhteistyön puitteissa toteutettavia hankkeita. Tieteellinen toiminta voi pitää sisällään mitä tahansa hankintajärjestelmän kohteen mukaista tutkimustoimintaa ja palveluita, mutta näissä palveluissa korostuu aina tieteellinen ja tutkimuksellinen näkökulma. Palvelut ja tutkimustoiminta voivat olla sellaisia, joista saatava hyöty koituu muidenkin kuin hankintayksikön toiminnassa käytettäväksi. Tiedeyhteisöiltä hankittavat palvelut voivat olla myös sellaisia tutkimus- ja kehittämispalveluita, joista saatava hyöty koituu yksinomaan hankintayksikön toiminnassa käytettäväksi ja hankintayksikkö korvaa suoritetun palvelun kokonaan. Palvelun luonne täsmennetään kussakin hankintajärjestelmän sisäisessä tarjouskilpailussa. Tiedeyhteisöiltä voidaan tilata palveluja myös suoraan ilman hankintajärjestelmän sisäistä kilpailutusta, mikäli hankintalain tutkimus- ja kehittämispalveluja koskevan soveltamisalapoikkeuksen (9 § 1 mom. 13-kohta) edellytykset täyttyvät. signals.description: Udbudsprocessen omfatter en kontrakt til Ordregivers anskaffelse af levering, implementering, drift, vedligeholdelse og support af enterprise ressource planning (ERP) system. Anskaffelsen af et enterprise ressource planning system er et led i Ordregivers nye strategi om at skabe en større grad af ensartethed på it-området på tværs af Ordregivers organisation med henblik på at realisere både økonomiske og kvalitetsmæssige fordele. ”Ensartethed” betyder ikke, at alle enheder i organisationen skal anvende identiske løsninger, men at it-beslutninger træffes på baggrund af fælles principper, procedurer og retningslinjer. På den måde sikres sammenhæng, standardisering hvor det er muligt, og fleksibilitet hvor det er nødvendigt. Formålet med en anskaffelse af et nyt ERP-system er således at opnå en højere grad at standardisering og harmonisering af processer på tværs af organisationen. Dette skal sikre enklere arbejdsgange, reduceret kompleksitet og en mere omkostningseffektiv drift. Ordregiver ønsker, at det nye ERP-system tilbyder tidssvarende teknologiske muligheder, herunder understøttelse af maskinlæring (ML), kunstig intelligens (AI) og andre værktøjer, der kan bidrage til øget automatisering og beslutningsstøtte. Ligeledes er let adgang til ny funktionalitet via løbende opgraderinger et centralt ønske, så organisationen hurtigt kan udnytte nye muligheder uden omfattende tilpasninger. ERP-systemet skal fungere som den centrale kerne i organisationens transaktionslag, hvor alle væsentlige data og processer samles og håndteres. Dette skal sikre datakonsistens, transparens og understøtte et integreret økosystem af omkringliggende applikationer. Den årlige værdi af kontrakten er anslået til tre (3) millioner DKK ekskl. moms. Hertil kommer en engangsimplementering med en forventet omkostning på tre (3) millioner DKK ekskl. moms. Kontraktens varighed er sat til 10 år, hvilket giver en samlet estimeret kontraktværdi på 33 millioner DKK ekskl. moms. Den samlede volumen er alene vejledende og baseret på historiske data og kan derfor ikke betragtes som en garanti for fremtidig omsætning.

signals.description: UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. Lot 1: . University College London Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust, "UCLH", is one of the largest NHS trusts in the United Kingdom and provides first-class acute and specialist services. UCLH comprises of the following hospitals: University College Hospital, Elizabeth Garrett Anderson Wing, MacMillan Cancer Centre, University College Hospital Grafton Way Building, University College Hospital at Westmoreland Street, Royal National ENT and Eastman Dental Hospitals, National Hospital for Neurology and Neurosurgery, Hospital for Tropical Diseases, Royal London Hospital for Integrated Medicine, and the Institute of Sport, Exercise and Health. UCLH delivers world class cancer care to patients from across the country. Cancer at UCLH spans across multiple sites and departments within the Trust and has included the opening of the Grafton Way Building one of two national Proton Beam Therapy services in December 2021. UCLH is a lead provider within the North Central London Cancer Alliance, as well as providing tertiary services for wider patient populations in specialist services, such as sarcoma for patients from across South East England. In early 2020, UCLH was selected by NHS England as the preferred tertiary cancer provider to take over management of the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre. This transition is subject to a due diligence process during which UCLH are providing transitional support to the Mount Vernon Cancer Centre team, building upon a number of years of collaborative working between the two services. Our Radiotherapy department offers cutting edge and specialised therapy to adult and paediatric patients treating over 2400 new patients a year. UCLH Radiotherapy is a national leader in complex/highly technical radiotherapy in: • Brain and was recently designated a Tessa Jowell Brain Cancer Centre of Excellence • Paediatrics, with the largest paediatric radiotherapy unit in the UK • Sarcomas - one of Europe’s largest service • Head and Neck – (ENT) third largest in the UK • Stereotactic Ablative Radiotherapy (SABR) • Haematological including total body radiation • Brachytherapy • Molecular Radiotherapy - National Referral centre (Paediatric, TYA and adult). The department works closely with a number of specialist hospitals to support cancer pathways which span multiple centres including Great Ormond Street, St. Mary's, Oxford, Southampton and the Royal National Orthopaedic Hospital. The UCH radiotherapy department contains six bunkers with four Varian TrueBeams and one Varian Halcyon. There is a large difference between the national and UCLH complexity profile, 92% of the UCH workload is classed as complex and approximately 8% of the workload is paediatric. The radiotherapy service is delivered by a team of staff including clinical oncologists, radiotherapy physics and engineers, therapeutic radiographers, healthcare play specialists, admin and clerical staff and dedicated nurses. UCLH is also one of two national Proton Beam Therapy centres, providing services to patients from the south of the UK. The departments run an integrated workforce model, with physicists, dosimetrists and radiographers rotating across Radiotherapy and PBT. In total there are around 300 WT across both services. UCLH wishes to procure a transformation partner to improve efficiency and productivity of the radiotherapy department, challenging current ways of working and offering new insights. This could include but is not limited to: • Delivering Cancer Waiting Time Access standards. • Scheduling of patients. • Machine downtime. • Patient pathway and organisation of workflow. • Radiotherapy physics pathways. • Process for commissioning of new linacs. • Use of automation and AI. Expression of Interest The purpose of this preliminary market engagement is to engage with potential partners to gather information and insights from the market to aid the development of the requirements and scope of opportunities for efficiencies to inform the procurement of a transformation partner. Suppliers are requested to provide expressions of interest, including responses to the below questions by e-mail to steviejay.cavanagh@nhs.net by 15:00 on 26th September 2025. 1. What innovative or new ways of working are you currently seeing in the market that may benefit the NHS, and more specifically UCLH, including those that have been included in procurements over the past 12 months? 2. Please describe how you think this contract should be best structured to deliver an efficient Radiotherapy service? 3. Is there anything you think that the Trust should consider before going out to market for these services? 4. What would be your expectations from a partnership with an NHS organisation? This notice does not constitute a formal call for competition. signals.description: The overall goal of this program is to accelerate scientific discovery, improve research efficiency, and enhance the translation of research findings into improved health outcomes. Centers funded under this program will also foster multidisciplinary collaboration, support workforce development across career stages, and promote training in emerging areas such as data science, artificial intelligence, and implementation research. The National Institute of Arthritis and Musculoskeletal and Skin Diseases (NIAMS) requests applications for the NIAMS P30 Centers Program to support integrated research Centers within its mission areas of skin biology and diseases; bone, muscle, and orthopaedic research; and rheumatic diseases. The NIAMS P30 Centers Program supports Centers that provide coordinated research infrastructure, shared resources, and methodological expertise to advance basic, translational, and clinical research. These Centers are expected to integrate state-of-the-art research resources with capabilities that support clinical and translational research, including the development, testing, and dissemination of novel analytical methods, study designs, outcome measures, and data-driven approaches. The overall goal of this program is to accelerate scientific discovery, improve research efficiency, and enhance the translation of research findings into improved health outcomes. Centers funded under this program will also foster multidisciplinary collaboration, support workforce development across career stages, and promote training in emerging areas such as data science, artificial intelligence, and implementation research.

signals.description: The purpose of this combined Broad Agency Announcement (BAA) under Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) Part 35 and Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) under 2 Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) 200.204 (henceforth referred to as “BAA”) is to solicit research proposals for submission to the U.S. Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) for funding consideration. This Broad Agency Announcement (BAA), for the Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C), is issued under the provisions of paragraph 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), which provides for the acquisition of basic, applied, and advanced research and that part of development not related to the development of a specific system or hardware procurement. This will be done through the competitive selection of proposals, and 10 U.S.C. 4001, 10 U.S.C. 4021, and 10 U.S.C. 4022, which provide the authorities for issuing awards under this announcement for basic, applied, and advanced research. The definitions of basic and applied research may be found at 32 CFR 22.105. Proposals submitted in response to this BAA and selected for award are considered to be the result of full and open competition and in full compliance with the provisions of Public Law 98-369, "The Competition in Contracting Act of 1984" and subsequent amendments. The Army Artificial Intelligence Integration Center (AI2C) is seeking artificial intelligence research and development whitepapers and proposals in support of new technologies and translational research-based approaches that support the identification, alignment, and exploitation of basic, applied, and advanced research. AI2C’s foundational research mission spans basic research (budget activity 6.1) and applied research (budget activity 6.2) as defined by 32 CFR 22.105 but may include advanced technology development (budget activity 6.3) and advanced component development and prototypes (budget activity 6.4) when opportunities arise to directly or indirectly help achieve AI2C’s mission. This publication constitutes a BAA for awards as contemplated in FAR 6.102(d)(2) and 35.016 as well as a merit-based, competitive procedure in accordance with the Department of Defense Grant and Agreement Regulations (DoDGARS) at 32 CFR 22.315(a) and the Office of the Under Secretary of Defense for Acquisition and Sustainment Other Transaction Guide version 2.0 dated July 2023.

signals.description: Complex generic drug products represent an increasing share of the generic marketplace and may have distinct user interface differences compared to reference listed drug (RLD) products. A modernized post-market surveillance approach is needed to compare clinical outcomes between complex generic products and their corresponding RLD products to monitor for potential issues with therapeutic equivalence and to inform regulatory decision making. Real-world data (RWD) combined with machine learning (ML) and/or artificial intelligence (AI) could help to identify post-market signals efficiently in an automated and repeatable fashion, facilitating timely regulatory action. The purpose of this funding opportunity is to develop and test an AI- or ML-based algorithmic RWD model for post-market surveillance of complex generic drug products.

This means that the NIH or FDA will not accept:•A new (A0) application that is submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of an overlapping new (A0) or resubmission (A1) application.•A resubmission (A1) application that is submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous new (A0) application.•An application that has substantial overlap with another application pending appeal of initial peer review (see 2.3.9.4 Similar, Essentially Identical, or Identical Applications).

signals.description: Birmingham City Council (the Council) is seeking to commission a specialist behavioural science consultancy to design and deliver a comprehensive behavioural systems model to understand the drivers of car and vehicle dependency across Birmingham and determine targets for behavioural interventions. This work will directly support the development and implementation of the city’s Healthy Streets programme, which aims to shape neighbourhoods that are safer, easier to navigate, and more pleasant to live in by supporting greater use of walking, cycling and public transport, and decreasing dependence on private vehicles. Vehicle dependency is a multifaceted behavioural challenge influenced by numerous interacting factors, such as habits, feelings of safety and ease, access to transport options, and broader environmental and societal influences. To address this complexity, BCC requires a robust, evidence‐informed modelling approach capable of identifying the most influential behavioural drivers and the highest‐impact opportunities for change. The Council will be using its free to use e-tendering system (in-tend) for the administration of this procurement process and potential suppliers must register with the system to be able to express an interest. signals.description: Introduction and Summary of Requirements DESNZ is looking for experts in their field with a strong network of contacts across their industry to act as an Alternate Delegate for the following International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programmes (TCPs): Lot 1 Energy Storage (ES) Lot 2 Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT) Lot 3 Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) Lot 4 Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) Summary UK Shared Business Services Ltd (UK SBS), acting on behalf of the Department for Energy Security and Net Zero (DESNZ), invites proposals for the role of Alternate Delegate for provision of support to the International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programme (TCP). UK SBS is managing this procurement process in accordance with the Procurement Act 2023 (PA 2023) and the Procurement Regulations 2024 applicable to this procurement procedure (as may be amended from time to time) (the “Regulations”). This is a Services Contract being procured under the Open Procedure. This procurement shall be split into 4 Lots as follows and for each Lot one Contract shall be awarded to the successful supplier(s). LOT 1 - Energy Storage (ES) LOT 2 - Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT) LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) LOT 4 - Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) Please state clearly which lot you are applying for in your submission in the bid title. The application must be submitted by an organisation for a specific individual within the organisation. This can be a company, university, NGO or sole trader. An organisation may submit bids for several lots, no single individual may be proposed for more than one Lot. For example, a Supplier may bid for all four Lots; however, a different academic or employee must be nominated as the lead representative for each Lot. Each lot will be assessed individually so please provide a separate application for each lot applied for (including declarations). Each lot will only be awarded to one bidder. Background The IEA works to ensure reliable, affordable and clean energy for its 32 member countries and beyond. Founded in 1974, the IEA was initially designed to help countries co-ordinate a collective response to major disruptions in the supply of oil, such as the crisis of 1973/4. While this remains a key aspect of its work, the IEA has evolved and expanded. It is at the heart of global dialogue on energy innovations. Technology Collaboration Programmes (TCPs) are independent, international groups of experts that enable governments and industries from around the world to lead programmes and projects on a wide range of energy technologies and related issues. TCPs currently cover topics related to: • Efficient end-use (buildings, electricity, industry, transport). • Cleaner fossil fuels (greenhouse-gas mitigation, extraction, supply, transformation). • Renewable energy and hydrogen (technologies and policies for deployment). • Cross-cutting issues (modelling, technology transfer, project financing). • Fusion power (safety, physics, materials, technologies). The 6,000 experts in the TCPs work to advance the research, development and commercialisation of energy technologies. The scope and strategy of each TCP is in keeping with the IEA Shared Goals of energy security, environmental protection and economic growth, as well as engagement worldwide. Depending on the TCP, activities may include: • Basic and applied research, technology development and pilot plants • Technology assessment, feasibility studies, environmental impact studies, market analysis, policy implications • Information exchange of research results and programmes • Scientist exchanges • Databases, modelling and systems analysis • Experts’ networks. More information on the IEA and the TCPs is available here: Technology collaboration - About - IEA. Each TCP typically has two Delegates who represent each country at the Executive Committee: a primary Delegate and an Alternate Delegate. Each TCP is its own entity and therefore have different methods for organising activities. The types of activities are, however, broadly consistent across the TCPs. The UK is currently participating in 28 TCPs. The Science and Innovation for Climate and Energy (SICE) directorate in DESNZ funds 12 of these. At this time, DESNZ is looking to appoint Alternate Delegates for 4 of these TCPs to represent the UK industry alongside the primary DESNZ Delegate: • Energy Storage - https://iea-es.org/ • Heat Pump Technologies (HPT) - http://www.heatpumpingtechnologies.org • Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) - https://iea-pvps.org/ • Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) - https://iea-industry.org/ The UK also participates in Mission Innovation, which is the leading international collaboration platform on innovation hosted by the IEA. SICE currently coordinates input into the seven Missions of Mission Innovation. Where relevant to the programme of work of the IEA Technology Collaboration Programmes, alternate delegates should seek to join up activities and stakeholder engagement. Acronyms and terminology: IEA TCP International Energy Agency (IEA) Technology Collaboration Programmes (TCPs): multilateral working groups established by the IEA across 8 themes (Buildings, Electricity, Industry, Transport, Renewable Energy, Fossil Energy, Fusion Power, cross-cutting) IEA TCP Secretariat Organises the general TCP administration (requesting invoices, organising annual activities), liaises with the IEA and stakeholders DESNZ (Primary) Delegate Government representative in the IEA TCPs. Drawn from across technical and policy teams. Primarily responsible for administration and knowledge transfer within DESNZ, quality assessment of UK outputs to IEA, but can get more involved depending on expertise and resource. Alternate Delegate (AD) Experts in their field appointed through open competition. In charge of running the UK’s TCP activities and producing main outputs. DESNZ TCP Co-ordinator Oversees all the TCPs at a working level within DESNZ and is responsible for the procurement of DESNZ and Alternate Delegates, reporting of TCP activities for DESNZ governing procedures and any general admin tasks not specific to individual TCPs. National TCP Coordinator Oversees all UK TCP Activity across 28 TCP Programmes with UK representation. Facilitates engagement across TCP representatives and provides support on alignment between TCPs and policy. Tasks / Annexes Sub-tasks produced by TCPs, where members create working groups to produce reports, gather international data on technologies/policies/ business models, etc. Known variously as tasks, sub-tasks, working groups, and annexes in different TCPs, but referred to as ‘annexes’ for clarity in this specification. Operating agent Project manager or technical lead of an annex. In charge of defining the programme of work of the annexes, and ensuring delivery of outputs. Known under different terminology across TCPs, but used here for clarity. National Team A team of UK experts from industry, third sector and academia convened by the Alternate Delegate. ExCo Executive committee meeting which typically occurs twice a year (generally at least once in person). The role of Alternate Delegate has general tasks common to all TCPs. Additional opportunities such as active participation in annex work or chairing the TCP can vary and be shaped by the AD and DESNZ Delegate. All ADs are expected to be able to complete all tasks, and the general tasks below are considered a minimum requirement. The Programme of Work will vary by TCP and will be jointly agreed with the DESNZ Delegate. The minimum requirement is expected to correspond to 12 days per financial year, amounting to a total minimum time requirement over the maximum potential duration of the contract of 29 days. Lot LOT 1 - Energy Storage (ES): LOT 1 - Energy Storage (ES). LOT 1 - Energy Storage (ES) The Alternate Delegate for the Energy Storage TCP will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the Energy Storage TCP. The Energy Storage TCP’s mission is “to facilitate integral research, development, implementation, and integration of energy storage technologies in order to raise the efficiency of all types of energy system and promote an increasing use of renewables over fossil fuels”. The TCP is an international community of policy makers, academics, and industry professionals working on all aspects of energy storage. This includes tasks on electrical, thermal, chemical, mechanical energy storage; integration of energy storage with energy systems; energy storage materials and components; and other related areas of work. Further information can be found here: Energy Storage Technology Collaboration Programme - IEA ES TCP Country Members: Austria, Belgium, Canada, China, Czechia, Denmark, European Union, Finland, France, Germany, Israel, Italy, Japan, South Korea, The Netherlands, Norway, Slovenia, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Turkey, United Kingdom, USA The general tasks are: • Represent the UK in ExCo Meetings. • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and the TCP. • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. Aims and Objectives The primary aims of this commission are to ensure that: • The activities of the TCPs are fully disseminated to their respective UK industries and researchers. • The UK takes an active role in the participation, management and development of the TCPs and ensures their activities are beneficial for the UK. • Activities across related TCPs are joined up, to avoid duplication and maximise added value through collaboration. Lot LOT 2 - Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT): LOT 2 - Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT). LOT 2 - Heat Pumping Technologies (HPT) The Alternate Delegate for the Heat Pumping Technologies TCP will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the HPT TCP. The HPT TCP is a non-profit organization working in the field of heat pumping technologies, i.e., all technologies where heat is lifted from a lower temperature level to a higher one, such as heat pumps, air conditioning, and refrigeration. Under the management of an Executive Committee representing the member countries, the programme carries out a strategy to accelerate the use of heat pumping technologies in all applications where they can reduce energy consumption, increase the use of renewable energy sources, and contribute to energy security and affordable energy for all – for the benefit of people, the environment, and a sustainable future. The main activities within the programme are to run collaborative research, development, demonstration, and deployment projects, to organise a triennial conference, and to perform communication through the Heat Pump Centre, the Projects, and the National teams. Further detail of the HPT TCP can be found here: https://heatpumpingtechnologies.org/ Participating countries are: Austria, Belgium, Canada, China, the Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, France, Italy, Ireland, Germany, Japan, the Netherlands, Norway, South Korea, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the United Kingdom, and the United States. The general tasks are: • Represent the UK in ExCo Meetings. • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and the TCP. • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. Aims and Objectives The primary aims of this commission are to ensure that: • The activities of the TCPs are fully disseminated to their respective UK industries and researchers. • The UK takes an active role in the participation, management and development of the TCPs and ensures their activities are beneficial for the UK. • Activities across related TCPs are joined up, to avoid duplication and maximise added value through collaboration. Lot LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS): LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS). LOT 3 - Photovoltaic Power Systems (PVPS) The Alternate Delegate for the PVPS TCP will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the PVPS TCP. The PVPS TCP conducts joint projects in the application of photovoltaic conversion of solar energy to electricity. This includes tasks related to PV sustainability activities, reliability and performance, transport, off-grid and edge-of-grid PV, and building-integrated PV. The IEA PVPS programme aims to realise its mission through the following objectives: • PV technology development • Competitive PV markets • An environmentally and economically sustainable PV industry • Policy recommendations and strategies • Impartial and reliable information Country members: Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, China, Denmark, European Union, Finland, France, Germany, India, Israel, Italy, Japan, Korea, Lithuania, Malaysia, Morocco, the Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Solar Energy Research Institute of Singapore (SERIS), Solar Power Europe, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Thailand, Türkiye, United Kingdom and United States of America. The general tasks are: • Represent the UK in ExCo Meetings. • Act as the primary liaison between UK industry and the TCP. • Prepare national annual reports for the IEA on the state of research, technology deployment, policy support and projects. • Manage and develop the National Team of interested experts, to coordinate tasks and knowledge dissemination. • Participate in and propose TCP tasks or annexes, which are working groups aimed at delivering a specific task or output, advancing the knowledge base of the relevant TCP area. • Knowledge transfer from the TCP to DESNZ through the DESNZ Delegate. • Prepare a short annual report summarising TCP activities for DESNZ’s monitoring and reviewing purposes in collaboration with the DESNZ Delegate. • Essential Lot 3 Requirements • Demonstrable expertise in solar PV technologies and the UK PV sector, and a strong understanding of PV deployment, policy, regulation and market developments in the UK • Ability to provide a strategic perspective on PV within the broader context of renewable energy deployment and the energy transition • Good understanding of key UK PV stakeholders across government, industry and academia • Ability to utilise relevant official databases and statistics to support reporting and analysis The following would be advantageous: • Access to commercial market intelligence and PV market databases. In addition, for Lot 3 (PVPS TCP) The Alternate Delegate is expected to participate in Task 1 (Strategic PV Analysis and Outreach): https://iea-pvps.org/research-tasks/strategic-pv-analysis-outreach/ Task 1 produces at least two reports or special events annually, highlighting key drivers and status of PV development in both IEA PVPS countries and globally. Current discussions focus on PV integration in mature markets including grid constraints, flexibility, curtailment, negative pricing, and the role of storage and demand-side measures. The Task also examines policy and regulatory challenges associated with PV deployment, supply chains, manufacturing competitiveness and the translation of technical evidence into policy and regulatory action. The core activities in this task are: • Attend twice yearly physical meetings. These meetings are the primary forum for discussion and decision-making, including agreement on deliverables, events and future activities. Each meeting is minimum 2.5 days. • Complete the annual national data collection exercise (PV deployment, market trends, costs, policies and grid integration) for the Snapshot of Global PV Markets and Trends in Photovoltaic Applications reports. • Review documents produced by the Task Other activities may include: • Participation to additional workshops in international conferences organized by IEA-PVPS Task 1 • Participation to the writing of additional reports. • Organising Task 1 meetings • Working with Task 15 Manager to organise and deliver an international workshop/seminar (virtual) on plug-in solar PV, including contributing to the preparation of any associated report or publication. Aims and Objectives The primary aims of this commission are to ensure that: • The activities of the TCPs are fully disseminated to their respective UK industries and researchers. • The UK takes an active role in the participation, management and development of the TCPs and ensures their activities are beneficial for the UK. • Activities across related TCPs are joined up, to avoid duplication and maximise added value through collaboration. Lot LOT 4 - Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS): LOT 4 - Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS). LOT 4 – Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS TCP) The Alternate Delegate for the IETS TCP (known as Industry TCP) will support in ensuring the UK derives value from participation in the Industry TCP and a similar initiative called the Net Zero Industries Mission. IEA Industrial Energy-Related Technologies and Systems (IETS) Technology Collaboration Programme (TCP) (known as Industry TCP): IETS | An IEA Technology Collaboration Programme The Industry TCP is coordinated by the Swedish Energy Agency and was launched in 2005. The programme is now wide ranging, covering industrial symbiosis, biorefineries, electrification, reuse of waste heat, AI, resilience to climate change, and circularity. At bi-annual Executive Committee Meetings government appointed delegates meet from each country to review updates on latest developments and share updates on policy and industry in their countries. The objective is to allow countries to work together to foster international co-operation for accelerated research and technology development of industrial energy-related technologies and systems with main focus on end-use technologies. The work is organised in Tasks, which can be viewed here: Tasks | IETS Country members: Austria, Canada, Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Sweden, Switzerland, UK; Sponsors (university or industry): Japan, Ireland, Finland, Spain, Belgium Mission Innovation – Net Zero Industries Mission (NIM): Net-Zero Industries Mission Mission Innovation is the leading intergovernmental platform for collaboration on Innovation, launched at COP21 by world leaders when the Paris Agreement was signed, recognising the need for innovation to meet Net Zero goals. NIM’s goal is to develop and demonstrate cost competitive solutions for the efficient decarbonization of energy intensive industries by 2030. The mission was launched in 2021 and is relatively new, with room to shape the activities based on UK interest. Country members: Australia, Austria, Canada, China, European Commission, Finland, Germany, Republic of Korea, UK, Switzerland. signals.description: We know that the structure of taxes shapes decisions about how and what to invest in. To better understand the incentives around the reuse of historic buildings, this study will look at how tax impacts on the finances of reuse projects, how the tax impacts differ depending on the type of project or developer, what the implications are for cash flow vs total financial impacts, and where the incidence of tax may be different to where the liability falls. signals.description: Digital Care Hub is seeking an independent evaluation partner to assess the delivery, impact, sustainability and value for money of the Better Security, Better Care (BSBC) programme. Funded by the Department of Health and Social Care, BSBC supports approximately 28,000 CQC-registered adult social care locations in England to improve cyber security, data protection and information governance, including compliance with the Data Security and Protection Toolkit (DSPT). Delivery is led nationally by Digital Care Hub through more than 30 Local Support Organisations, combining central leadership, guidance, training, communications, data analysis and performance management with trusted local support. The supplier will design and deliver a proportionate mixed-method evaluation covering programme governance and delivery, stakeholder engagement, partner effectiveness, reach, changes in awareness and behaviour, adoption of good practice, DSPT outcomes, organisational resilience, wider benefits, cost effectiveness, return on investment and social and economic value. The work should identify lessons, good practice and evidence-based recommendations while providing ongoing insight to support continuous improvement. Key deliverables are an evaluation framework and inception report within three months; ongoing data collection, analysis and stakeholder engagement; monthly progress meetings; an interim report by September 2027; and a final evaluation report, shorter executive report, presentation and dissemination-ready outputs by October 2028. Close-down and dissemination support will continue to March 2029. The proposed contract runs from October 2026 to March 2029, with a maximum budget of £125,000 inclusive of VAT. Bidders must demonstrate strong experience in programme and economic evaluation, publicly funded programmes, mixed-method research, stakeholder engagement and report writing. Knowledge of adult social care, health and care systems, cyber security, digital transformation or information governance is required. Tender responses must include organisation and personnel details, methodology, data collection and analysis plans, delivery timetable, resourcing, quality assurance, risk management, up to three relevant examples, a full pricing schedule, assumptions and proposed social value. Evaluation weightings are: understanding 15%, methodology 35%, experience 20%, project management 10%, social value 10% and price 10%. The supplier must comply with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018, confidentiality, insurance, procurement, equality and safeguarding requirements. Clarification questions are due by 14 October 2026 and tenders by 18 October 2026. Please see attachment for full specifications.

signals.description: Kent Fire and Rescue Service (KFRS) is exploring options for a Project Portfolio Management (PPM) solution to support the planning, management, oversight and reporting of projects and programmes across the organisation. KFRS is open to different solution and delivery models, including established Software as a Service (SaaS) products and Microsoft/Power Platform-based solutions. Please note: For the purposes of this market engagement, KFRS is only seeking responses in respect of solutions which are currently available for procurement through an existing Government Commercial Agency (GCA) framework (formerly CCS). Suppliers should identify the relevant framework, Lot (where applicable) and service/solution listing within their response. The purpose of this exercise is to undertake a short and proportionate test of the market before KFRS determines its procurement strategy and route to market. In particular, KFRS wishes to understand: •what potentially suitable solutions are available within or around the stated affordability envelope; •the broad alignment of available products with KFRS's functional and technical requirements; •the different solution and service models available and the respective responsibilities of KFRS and the supplier; •indicative licensing/subscription, implementation, support and ongoing configuration/development costs; •the extent to which solutions allow KFRS to retain appropriate control and portability of its organisational data; •any observations from the market which may help KFRS refine its requirements; and •the specific GCA/CCS framework, Lot and/or service listing through which the proposed solution can be procured. Nature of this Exercise This is a preliminary market engagement exercise and not a competitive procurement or invitation to tender. The functional and technical requirements provided with this brief represent KFRS's current understanding of its needs. They are being provided to give suppliers sufficient information to determine whether they have a product or solution that could potentially meet the requirement. Suppliers are not required to provide a detailed response against each individual requirement or complete the requirements schedules on a line-by-line basis. Responses will not be evaluated or scored as tender submissions. Instead, KFRS is seeking a brief, high-level response that will enable us to understand whether a proposed solution appears sufficiently aligned with our needs to warrant further exploration. KFRS would also welcome constructive feedback on the requirements themselves. This may include identifying areas which would benefit from clarification, or alternative approaches or current market capabilities which KFRS should consider. Please respond via the Kent Business Portal. Additional information: The contracting authority considers that this contract may be suitable for economic operators that are small or medium enterprises (SMEs). However, any selection of tenderers will be based solely on the criteria set out for the procurement.
